correctness.rationale: For t=1 and t=2, edges of the 4-state and 16-state de Bruijn graphs correspond bijectively to length-3 and length-5 input windows. Every length-n output word has such a path if and only if it is in F^t of the bilateral full shift. Subset-mask transitions recognize this language for every n. Exhaustive BFS of paired masks proves no discrepancy for 72 rules, with all reachable states closed, or finds a provably shortest word for 184; the maximum reported shortest length is 12 with exact histogram and two witnesses. All computations are reproduced by included verify.py and the generated classification.csv; a separate enumeration of finite input blocks checks all 256 rules for n=1,...,5, every shortest witness and both extremal n=12 cases. No finite-experiment-to-infinite inference is used: the exhaustive automaton closure supplies the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: Ballier (arxiv:1301.3790v1) develops general stable cellular automata but not elementary-rule first-vs-second-image counts or shortest witnesses. De Oliveira et al. (doi:10.1002/cplx.21686) publicly supply the general finite-time graph technique, explicitly Rule 126 graphs at t=1 and t=2, and a graph-size complexity table, but their conclusion calls for future time-difference comparisons. Thus graph machinery and related Rule 126 data are prior; the global 72/184 language-equality census, complete shortest-witness histogram, and sharp maximum twelve over all 256 rules are not stated or forced by those published tables. Nearby indexed studies concern different CA families or individual rules. Residual priority risk: unindexed exhaustive earlier table.
residual_risks: The 2015 Rule 126 two-step graph could imply the individual extremal witness by a further calculation; novelty is claimed for the complete global sharp theorem, not its primitive graph data.
An unindexed exhaustive enumeration or supplementary table could predate this classification.
The 2017 selected-rules follow-up was not accessible in full, and its uninspected sections might bear on individual-rule results.

value.rationale: A natural dynamical distinction is whether a cellular automaton already surjects onto its own one-step image and hence stabilizes that image forever; a second natural observable is the first finite output window that detects additional loss of admissible configurations. The complete family-level 72/184 partition and the sharp 12-window maximum supply new exact invariants, including two uniquely extremal rules. A global maximum is not implied by separate illustrative examples or routine one-step forbidden-language computations.
